Large language models (LLMs) can often tell when they are being tested. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages. Indic languages are spoken by over a billion people, yet evaluation awareness remains almost entirely unstudied in them. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely adopted by systems and users across the world, and are increasingly relied upon to refuse harmful requests. Their training corpora are overwhelmingly skewed towards English, often exceeding 90% of pre-training and fine-tuning data ( Xu et al. , 2025), yet they serve users in many other languages. The standard way to ensure reliability is to test models under controlled conditions through safety evaluations. These evaluations assume that behavior under test carries over to deployment. We studied evaluation awareness in five Indic languages alongside English. A cue that signals a safety evaluation raises refusal of harmful prompts in every model and language. On average, the rise in Indic languages is at least as large as in English. Refusal rises even with a cue that never uses the words test or evaluation. A safety test that a model can recognize may therefore make Indic safety look better than it is.
